articles.title: Tony Gatlif obituary
articles.summary: Algerian-born French director of more than 20 films that celebrated Roma culture. The French film director Tony Gatlif, who has died aged 77, was regularly described as “cinema’s Gypsy auteur”, so often did his films focus on Roma communities and their music.
body: Latcho Drom conveys the centuries-long migration from Asia to western Europe of a nomadic people we now call Gypsies or Roma, as a fable told entirely in images and music. There is no voiceover, talking heads or text; instead Gatlif lets the striking settings and musical performances enchant viewers. It is an idealised portrait of the Roma, not a documentary (as some labelled it), and while Gatlif portrays the discrimination and persecution Roma communities experience, his emphasis was on celebrating Roma beauty and artistry.

After the success of Latcho Drom, Gatlif went on to write and direct a feature film every couple of years, his most recent being Ange (2025). These films were all dramas and tended to focus either on a Roma community – Mondo (1995), Gadjo Dilo (1997), Vengo (2000), Swing (2001), Korkoro (2009) – or were road movies in which the protagonists drift across France, then head into eastern Europe or North Africa, seeking meaning and origins. His 2004 film Exils won Gatlif the best director award at the Cannes film festival.
points: Algerian-born French director of more than 20 films that celebrated Roma culture.

articles.title: NAZA review – Israeli intelligence officers cast chilling light on civilian deaths
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Under the cover of night, anonymous personnel discuss AI, error rates and problematic intelligence units in a documentary produced by the Guardian.
body: There are flaws: interviews were conducted on the condition of anonymity, but if no-one can be persuaded to put their name and face to their words (and of course it is terribly dangerous) then the impact of this as testimony is lessened. But even so, the film is casting a chilling light on what is happening now in Gaza.

Their faces in shadow, appearances and voices digitally altered, disillusioned Israeli intelligence officers and personnel speak to the directors about the war in Gaza. They do this semi-furtively on the dark night-time rooftops of Tel Aviv, the home of Israeli intelligence, supposedly for journalistic secrecy purposes – but it also provides a dramatic backdrop, as well as ambient footage of the city in all its eerie heedlessness and heartlessness. Periodically, the camera’s eye will drift across the gleaming apartment buildings, zooming in on glimpses of prosperous lives just 60km from Gaza.

articles.title: The Odyssey and Spider-Man propel record-breaking summer box office worldwide
articles.summary: The biggest May to September of all time was recorded in US cinemas, with the UK enjoying a 56% rise in audiences, outstripped by an 88% lift in the Middle East and Africa.
body: As well as celebrating their wedding, the actors Tom Holland and Zendaya have something else to toast: their two summer blockbusters – The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day – have officially made box office history.
The films were credited as the driving force behind the US’s biggest summer season of all time, taking $4.761bn (£3.51bn) from 1 May-7 September, beating 2013’s $4.756bn.

Spider-Man is currently on $2.4bn worldwide and likely to climb higher, while The Odyssey has made $1.6bn. Other key titles driving sales include Toy Story 5, Michael and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, all of which have grossed over $1bn.

The breadth of the success of Destin Daniel Cretton’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day was a particular surprise. The film is the best-performing of the year so far and the third highest-grossing film of all time. Its opening weekend was the second-best of all time behind Avengers: Endgame (2019) and it is also the second-fastest film to gross $1bn, doing so in six days.

articles.title: Is ‘Vintage Violence’ the Future of Movies? Inside the Frantic Chase Movie Built for Phone-Addicted Audiences: It’s a ‘New Approach to Viewing’
articles.summary: Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence” is a movie that speaks directly to America’s phone-obsessed culture. The kinetic action adventure, which has its world premiere Sept.
body: Kotlyarenko, whose previous film was the similarly internet-minded 2020 thriller “Spree,” says the online style was essential for the story he wanted to tell.
Even though Kotlyarenko’s technique is extremely modern, he is comforted by knowing that some of cinema’s greats are also into pushing visual and tech boundaries.

“One of the great adventures and joys of trying to innovate something is using those cinematic techniques and finding inspiration in other filmmakers,” he says. “There are filmmakers who seem very technologically in tune, like Brian De Palma, or Pedro Almodóvar is always doing something that feels very contemporary technologically. So I’m looking to what’s cool about how the masters think about stuff and then trying to put my own energy and spin on it.”

Another important visual element came from nodding to Japanese film culture, as so much of the movie was shot there with a local crew. Kotlyarenko, along with his DP Sean Price Williams, was able to experiment in the footsteps of Japanese cinema legends.

articles.title: Nicholas Sparks’ ‘Counting Miracles’ Adaptation at Amazon to Be Helmed by ‘The Peanut Butter Falcon’ Filmmaker Tyler Nilson (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Amazon MGM Studios’ adaptation of the Nicholas Sparks bestseller “Counting Miracles” has found its writer/director in “The Peanut Butter Falcon” co-filmmaker Tyler Nilson.
body: Nilson’s breakout came with 2019’s “The Peanut Butter Falcon,” which he co-wrote and co-directed with Michael Schwartz as their feature debut. Starring Shia LaBeouf, Dakota Johnson and Zack Gottsagen, the film won the Audience Award at SXSW, earned a DGA nomination for Achievement in First-Time Feature Film, landed on the NBR’s Top Ten Independent Films list and became the highest-grossing indie release of the year.

Next up for Nilson was 2024’s “Los Frikis,” which he co-wrote and directed with Schwartz and was produced by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller. Starring Adria Arjona and Héctor Medina, the film was set in 1990s Cuba.

Best known for his novels including “The Notebook,” “A Walk to Remember,” “Message in a Bottle,” “Dear John,” “The Last Song,” “Safe Haven,” “The Longest Ride” and “The Choice,” Sparks is no stranger to a Hollywood adaptation. His novels have been made into films that have collectively grossed more than $750 million worldwide, with Sparks serving as a producer on several adaptations.
Aside from “Counting Miracles,” Sparks’ next big film adaptation is “Remain,” which stars Jake Gyllenhaal and is set to release Feb. 5, 2027.

articles.title: Two times a charm: Is Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman’s agelessness the real trick of Practical Magic 2?
articles.summary: A film about sisterhood with fifty- and sixtysomething female leads is something to cheer – but would it have been made if its stars had aged like mere mortals since the 1998 original?
body: Would Hollywood have brought Practical Magic back from the dead if the intervening 28 years looked more visible on Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman? An awkward question, as it risks subjecting their faces to the invasive scrutiny older female actors already endure. Their return as leads in their late 50s and early 60s should count as progress. Yet it reveals a condition of female stardom: age can increase a female actor’s nostalgic value, provided it does not show too clearly on her face.

In Practical Magic 2, Bullock, 62, and Kidman, 59, return as sisters Sally and Gillian Owens. Dianne Wiest, 78, and Stockard Channing, 82, are back too. Joey King and Maisie Williams play Sally’s adult daughters, but Sally and Gillian remain central.

As producers, Bullock and Kidman helped choose director Susanne Bier and protect the original’s tone. That creative influence is quite a reversal from 1998, when the film’s female cast and subject matter drew condescension. Bullock remembers being asked: “How many women do you need in a film?” Yet it became a cult favourite. The female world once dismissed as excessive became the source of its value.

articles.title: Esther Rantzen says she is too fragile to travel to Switzerland to end life
articles.summary: The broadcaster and campaigner says she missed her chance to go before living with cancer became "unbearable".
body: Dame Esther Rantzen has said she is now "too physically fragile" to travel to Switzerland to end her life at an assisted suicide clinic.

The veteran broadcaster, 86, said she would have to fly to the country, where the practice is legal, alone, which she could only have done before her life became "unbearable" and before she was ready to end her life.
The Childline founder, who is terminally ill with cancer, first revealed in December 2023 that she had joined the Dignitas clinic.

Dame Esther used her statement on Thursday to reiterate a plea for MPs to vote in favour of legalising assisted suicide in England and Wales when proposed legislation is revisited by Parliament on Friday.

articles.title: New Strictly hosts explain their roles as they reject 'roving presenter' reports
articles.summary: Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdicombe and Emma Willis say their roles are not "fixed" or defined.
body: Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Radebe have said they will not have "fixed roles" on Strictly Come Dancing, as they prepare to replace Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman later this month.
Daly and Winkleman left the programme together at the end of the 2025 series.
Daly was the host on the dancefloor, introducing the dancers and judges, while Winkleman did the post-dance debrief upstairs in the "Clauditorium".
"No one's replacing anybody - at the minute it's all very kind of open," Willis told Richard Osman on The Rest is Entertainment podcast.

articles.title: Charlie Hunnam Says ‘Legacy’ Spinoff Is “Definitely Not Season 8 of ‘Sons of Anarchy'”
articles.summary: The 'Monster' star reveals how the idea came to him for the meta-thriller that will bring back Jax Teller and the core characters of the beloved FX motorcycle drama.
body: News of Jax Teller’s revival was major. But if Charlie Hunnam had his way, the Sons of Anarchy surprise would have stayed secret for longer.

“My desire was to keep it as secret as possible, but there were a couple of very tenacious news organizations that had gleaned that we were doing something ( laughs ), so FX wanted to get out ahead of it,” Hunnam now tells The Hollywood Reporter about last month’s viral announcement about the Sons of Anarchy spinoff.

But it was revealed that the spinoff would actually feature the original cast playing fictionalized versions of themselves, the “real-life brotherhood” heading “on an adventure that is both a love letter to the series and a fun meta twist on what fans think they know.”
